## COMMENTS ON

INFORMATION ANXIETY

(FIRST EDITION)

One of the great information crafters gives sound counsel on how to craft your own damn information.

Stewart Brand, Co-Founder, Global Business Network; Author, The Whole Earth Catalog

Richard Saul Wurman has not only changed the way we think about processing information, he's changed the way books are going to be written. A must read for anyone who has to communicate in today's fast forward world. Jay Chiat, CEO, Screamingmedia.com

Richard Saul Wurman is the master of guidebooks—the greatest innovator in one of the most important and interesting genres in publishing. Guidebooks are sublime; they are not only maps to places, but optimal orderings of concepts—and therefore require the greatest originality in conception. What could be more valuable than a guidebook to instructions themselves in our information age?

Stephen Jay Gould, Author.

Evolution: The Pleasures of Pluralism;

Professor, Harvard University

I couldn't help but think as I read Information Anxiety that this book is at once obvious, profound, disquieting, and comforting. It's probably too much to say that I will never feel magazine guilt again, but at least I know that I'm in good company.

Nancye Green, Designer, Donovan & Green

Richard Saul Wurman's Information Anxiety is informative, stimulating, and original. In an age when all available information doubles every five years, this book will be a useful tool to help us separate the wheat from the chaff.

Vartan Gregorian, President,

Carnegie Corp. of New York

## Richard Saul Wurman

## Richard Saul Wurman

Richard Saul Wurman received both M. Arch. & B. Arch. degrees from the University of Pennsylvania. He established a deep personal and professional relationship with the architect Louis I. Kahn. He is a fellow of the American Institute of Architects (FAIA).

He has been awarded several grants from the National Endowment for the Arts, a Guggenheim Fellowship, two Graham Fellowships, and two Chandler Fellowships. In 1991, Richard Saul Wurman received the Kevin Lynch Award from MIT for his creation of the ACCESS travel guides, and was honored by a retrospective exhibition of his work at the AXIS Design Gallery in Tokyo, Japan on the occasion of its 10th anniversary. In 1996, the Pacific Design Center awarded him its Stars of Design Lifetime Achievement Award, and that same year he received the Chrysler Design Award. In 1993/1997 he was appointed as a Visiting Scholar at MIT in the Department of Architecture & Planning. He was awarded a Doctorate of Fine Arts by the University of the Arts in Philadelphia in 1994. In 1995, he received an Honorary Doctorate of Letters from Art Center College of Design. In 1997 & 1999 he was named one of the 100 elite of the technology industry by Upside magazine, and in 1999, he received an Honorary Doctorate of Fine Arts from the Art Institute of Boston.

His career has spanned from a 13-year architectural partnership in Philadelphia, a Director of GEE! (Group for Environmental Education) to teaching at Cambridge University, England, CCNY, UCLA, USC, Washington University in St. Louis, and Princeton University. In 1958, he was a member of the initial year of exploration at Tikal, Guatemala. Recently, he entered into a joint venture with Ovations, a UnitedHealth Group Company, to create a new publishing company called TOP, which publishes books and related media on health and wealth, where he is CEO and Creative Director. He has also been named a member of the Board of Directors of the International eBook Award Foundation.

## Loring Leifer

Loring Leifer became a writer because she likes to find things. She's uncovered art forgeries and discovered how many employees can name their company president, all in magazine articles and books. As president of WordsWorth a writing business in metro Kansas City, she helps clients find ways to make their communication materials more actionable and instructive. Leifer's credits include working on the original Information Anxiety, Follow the Yellow Brick Road, Younger Voices, Stronger Choices; and A Report Card on the Status of Children in Kansas City.

## David Sume

David Sume has worked with Richard Saul Wurman for more than six years. In the course of his efforts to help Richard execute projects based on his interests, he has been able to pursue many of his own eclectic interests.
